examples.scenario: SaaS free trial welcome sequence — 5 emails

input.goal: Convert trial users to paid ($29/mo) within 14 days
input.tone: Warm, smart, gets to the point

emails.theme: The fast start — get them to first value in 5 min
subject_lines: A: Your workspace is ready (5-min quick start inside)
B: The one thing to do in your first 5 minutes
C: Don't skip this — it determines whether this sticks
emails.preview_text: Most people skip this and regret it later.
emails.body:
Your trial just started. Here's the one thing that separates people who love this 30 days later from people who don't:

Create your first real project — not a test project, not 'sandbox' — something you're actually working on.

[→ Start your first real project](link)

Takes 4 minutes. And everything clicks once you have real data in it.

I'll be here if you have questions.

— [Name]
Founder, [Product]

P.S. Reply to this email. Seriously — I read every one.
emails.notes: Plain text only. Founder signature builds trust. Encourage replies — this is also research.

emails.theme: The aha moment — show them the thing that changes how they work
subject_lines: A: The feature product teams use 100x more than they expected
B: This is why our users stopped using Jira
C: Have you tried [Feature] yet?
emails.preview_text: It takes 90 seconds to set up. Most people don't find it on their own.
emails.body:
Most teams who try [Product] discover the [connected docs + tasks] feature by accident.

Then they reorganize their entire workflow around it.

Here's what it does:
You write a spec → tasks automatically link to it → when a developer comments on the task, it shows up in the spec.

One source of truth. No more Slack threads asking 'wait, which version is final?'

Set it up for one project right now:
[→ Connect my first doc to tasks](link)

It's the thing that makes the rest of it click.

— [Name]

P.S. Tomorrow I'll show you how [Company Name] used this to cut their weekly sync from 90 minutes to 20.
emails.cta: Connect my first doc to tasks →

emails.theme: Social proof + objection removal — they're starting to wonder if it's worth paying
subject_lines: A: How [Real Company] cut meeting time by 60% (specific story)
B: 'I was skeptical after Notion burned us' — what changed
C: The PM who almost cancelled her trial
emails.preview_text: She almost quit after day 2. Here's why she's still here at month 7.
emails.body:
Sarah was three days into her trial and ready to quit.

'It felt like Notion with extra steps,' she told me later.

Then her team had their first sprint planning in [Product].

Not a demo sprint. A real one, with real tickets, a real deadline, and four engineers who had no patience for broken tools.

Six months later, she's a paying customer, she's expanded from her team of 5 to her company of 80, and she wrote us a case study.

The specific thing that changed her mind? [Read the full story →](link)

(It's a 3-minute read. And if her situation sounds like yours, it'll probably change yours too.)

— [Name]

emails.theme: Value deepening — show them something they haven't discovered yet
subject_lines: A: The [Product] feature most teams find in month 3 (you can have it now)
B: 7 days in — have you tried this?
C: What your trial data tells us about your workflow
emails.preview_text: The power users all use this. Most people find it by accident.
emails.body:
One week in. Here's something the teams who get the most value always have in common:

They set up [Automation Feature].

Specifically: when a task moves to 'Done,' it automatically pings the relevant doc and logs a changelog entry.

Zero manual updates. Zero 'did you ship that?' Slack messages.

Here's how to set it up in 3 steps:
1. Go to Settings → Automations
2. Choose 'Task Status Change' trigger
3. Connect to your project doc

[→ Set up my first automation](link)

If this saves you 30 minutes a week, that's 26 hours this year.

— [Name]

P.S. Your trial ends in 7 days. Here's what's included in the paid plan: [link to pricing]
emails.notes: Soft pricing mention here — not pushy, but plant the seed.

emails.theme: The close — trial ends in 2 days
subject_lines: A: Your trial ends in 48 hours
B: Before you go — one question
C: 2 days left (and a question for you)
emails.preview_text: If it's not clicking, I want to know why.
emails.body:
Your trial ends in 2 days.

If [Product] has become part of how your team works — upgrading takes 90 seconds:
[→ Upgrade now — $29/month](link)

If it hasn't clicked yet, I'd genuinely like to know why.

Hit reply and tell me: what was supposed to work that didn't?

I ask because we've built every major feature based on exactly this kind of feedback. And if something's broken or missing for your use case, I want to know.

— [Name]

P.S. If you upgrade today, you get access to [Bonus Feature] that's launching next week. Early access for everyone who upgrades before Friday.
emails.segmentation: Non-openers after email 4: send re-engagement variant with subject 'Did this end up in the wrong inbox?'

input.trigger: Added to cart, no purchase after 1 hour

subject_lines: A: Still thinking it over?
B: You left something behind
C: Your cart is saved (for now)
emails.body:
Looks like life got in the way.

Your cart is still saved — your [Product Name] is waiting.

[→ Complete your order](link)

Any questions? Reply here — real humans answer within 2 hours.

subject_lines: A: This is what makes it different
B: Before you decide — one thing worth knowing
C: The question we get asked most before someone buys
emails.body:
The most common question we get before someone orders:

'Is it really worth $89 for a wallet?'

Honest answer: For most people, no. A $20 wallet holds cards.

But if you've ever had a wallet:
- Fall apart at the seams after 8 months
- Crack in cold weather
- Bulk up until it sits sideways in your pocket

This one doesn't do any of those things.

We use full-grain leather — the same grade used in quality belts and shoes that last decades. Not bonded leather. Not 'genuine leather' (which is the lowest possible grade). Full-grain.

And we back it with a lifetime warranty — if it ever fails, we replace it.

[→ Complete your order](link)

Or reply if you have questions.

subject_lines: A: Last call — your cart expires tonight
B: One final thing (then I'll stop)
C: This is the last one (I promise)
emails.body:
Cart expires at midnight tonight.

If the price was the hesitation — use FIRST10 for 10% off your first order.

[→ Claim 10% off now](link)

If it wasn't the price — no hard feelings. Let me know what held you back and I'll make sure we fix it for the next person.

— [Founder Name], [Brand]
emails.notes: Only use discount if margin allows. Test 'no discount' vs 'discount' version — often conversion rate is similar but margin is better without.
